title: A business owner's legal remedies against defamatory online reviews
p1:
One fake online review can cost a business far more than a bad day of sales.

But can a business owner actually take legal action against someone who posts damaging reviews online?
p2:
Here's a common misconception: Every negative review is defamatory. That's not true.

Customers are generally allowed to share honest opinions, even harsh criticism. However, deliberately false statements presented as facts, such as falsely accusing a business of fraud, cheating customers, or selling unsafe products, may cross the line into defamation.
p3:
So, what can a business owner do?

Start by preserving evidence. Take screenshots showing the review, username, date, and platform. Save relevant customer records and communications.

You can report the review to the platform, request its removal, and send a legal notice when appropriate. If the false statement has caused reputational or financial damage, filing a defamation lawsuit may also be an option.

One useful insight: You don't have to respond publicly to every damaging review. A calm response and properly preserved evidence may be far more valuable than an emotional online argument.

The exact remedies depend on the applicable state or country's laws.
conclusion: If someone posts a knowingly false review that damages your business, would you first report it to the platform or consider legal action? Share your thoughts.
